newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Spain cuts rate to 5.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Spain cuts rate to 5.25 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Spain lowered its key money market rate by 25 basis points to 5.25 percent on Friday as expected. Following are analysts comments:
ANTONIO MIELGO, ECONOMIST AT THE BANK OF AMERICA IN MADRID

"The Bank of Spain proved once again to be cautious in cutting only 25 basis points. This is also due to the fact that other central banks in Europe are so cautious. The Bank of Italy, for example, which has lower inflation, is keeping the rate higher. We believe the Bank of Spain can cut another 25 bps to 5.0 percent next month after May CPI. Then it will have another 25 basis points scope which it is likely to use in the last quarter of the year, in October or November. By then it will be clear how much inflation can pick up and the EMU picture will also be more clear. The market is strong, as are others in Europe, but the spread (over Bunds) at 80 basis points is offering a very strong resistance. There's more risk to a wider spread than of a smaller one."
HEAD OF ECONOMIC SERVICES AT COMMERCIAL BANK, UNQUOTABLE

"It was impossible for the Bank of Spain not to cut rates given such good inflation data for the month of April. We believe that there is margin for a cut of another 50 basis points, but the Bank of Spain should reserve a cut for the final quarter before the expected rise of external funds before the perception that Spain will enter in EMU."
FERNANDO GUTIERREZ, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT ARGENTARIA

"It was what was expected. I think the Bank of Spain has reserved another quarter point for next month if inflation, as it seems, continues to decelerate. For the rest of the year, there could be scope for another 25 basis points coinciding with the presentation of the budget or something similar."

"We were going for a 25 basis point cut after very good inflation data and the peseta has been stable. We think that if inflation stays below two percent in May and the peseta remains stable they could cut another 25 basis points to five percent. There is a possibility of it staying at five as inflation picks up later in the year. We've seen 12 cuts in the last 17 months. I think we'll see 13 in 18 but they can't go on forever."
WILLIAM THORNHILL, SENIOR ECONOMIST, TECHNICAL DAT

"They've got room to cut more. The inflation rate has less room to improve more than it had in the past. May CPI could fall to 1.4/1.5 percent but then it will increase from then. That will increase real interest rate to 3.85 percent versus a record low of 3.05 percent in December 1996. So they have plenty of room to cut if they wish. One question is how wise it is to cut more with the recovery under way. If this rate cut had a 90 percent probability the next cut at mid June has a 40 percent one.
